new_packages.proposed_label_en: Truth and the Light of God
new_packages.reason: This is the most extensively developed bechina cluster in Torah #112, and the Torah's structural center. The Rebbe declares explicitly (line 21) that 'הָאֱמֶת הוּא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ, וְהוּא בְּחִינוֹת: ה' אוֹרִי' — Truth IS a bechina of 'Hashem is my light'. The entire Teaching opens (lines 6-7) with the declaration that Truth is God's seal (חותמו), that it is 'ראש תוך סוף' (beginning-middle-end, the full alef-bet = the divine Name). From Truth flows the motif of the ark's illuminator צֹהַר: 'צֹהַר תַּעֲשֶׂה לַתֵּבָה — שֶׁתְּדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרֵי אֱמֶת הַמְּאִירִים'. The צוהר (illuminating skylight) IS the illuminating words of truth. Then Rashi's two opinions on צוהר are decoded as two gradations of the same truth-concept: the precious stone (אבן טוב) that self-illuminates = the person who has achieved true Truth (אמת האמיתי) and shines from within; the window (חלון) that receives external illumination = the person at a lower level of truth who can be illuminated by another. All five nodes share the same essential nature: they are all expressions of the divine luminosity that attaches to a person who walks in Truth.

Three levels: (1) דיבור נקרא אמה — speech IS called cubit; (2) אמה = אש מים (acronym) — the cubit's letters reveal speech is composed of fire and water; (3) the ה of אמה = the five articulation-points of the mouth. These all share the same nature: they are different angles on what speech essentially IS. The term נִקְרָא is the most explicit possible bechina marker in the Rebbe's language. This package is smaller but formally complete: it is a tight analytic unpacking of what speech IS at its root.

new_packages.merge_consideration: Package B (speech/cubit) could be merged into Package A (Truth/Light) because the Torah uses truthful speech (דיבורי אמת) as its central motif — the cubit IS the speech IS the truth-expression. Truth produces illuminating speech, but the cubit/speech is not the same as divine light — it is the vehicle. Per framework rules, one PRODUCES the other (eitza), so they should be kept separate. Recommend keeping as separate packages unless the review team judges the Torah too thin for this distinction to matter.

new_packages.reason: The second major thematic section of Torah #112 (lines 29-36) develops the structure of prayer's cosmic ascent. Three central bechina statements organize this section: (1) line 34: 'הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מִטָּתוֹ' — prayer IS a bechina of the bed/matteh; (2) line 31: 'וְקָם שֵׁבֶט מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל... שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַעֲלוֹת תְּפִלָּתוֹ לְשַׁעַר שִׁבְטוֹ' — the שבט (tribe/gate) is where prayer must go; (3) line 31: 'דָּרַךְ הוּא בְּחִינוֹת זִוּוּג' — the path IS a bechina of celestial union [already in dataset as edge 1047]. All of these share the same essential nature: they are expressions of the aligned, properly-channeled upward movement of prayer that produces divine union above. The מיטה (bed) = prayer because one's foundational resting-place corresponds to one's tribal alignment. The שבט (tribe) = the gate through which prayer ascends. The דרך (path/treading) = the זיווג (union) that prayer produces. The כוכב (star, from 'דרך כוכב מיעקב') is the image that unifies דרך and שבט in the same verse: the star's path from Jacob produces the tribal standing. This package extends the existing dataset Package 1 (דרך/זיווג) significantly — the existing dataset package should be absorbed into this larger package when the data is enriched.

observations:
Torah #112 is one of the most under-represented Torahs in the dataset. With only 1 bechina edge in the entire database, the existing package structure (1 two-node package) captures almost nothing of the Torah's rich conceptual architecture. The source text contains at minimum 12 additional nodes with explicit bechina language spread across 5 independent conceptual domains. 

The Torah's argument follows a clear two-part structure:

PART 1 (lines 1-28) — The core teaching on Truth and Prayer:
